description: Cost-parity study, expansion: 5 single GPT-5.6 Sol workers at xhigh on crowbook. A single worker is the build node alone, byte-identical to round 1 of luna-xhigh-crowbook-v1's loop (same prompt, environment, node and limits). Their mean cost sets the budget at which Luna's loop runs are compared (decision_rule.cost_parity).

task.adjustments_rationale: As in the svgbob experiments v2 to v5, the reference moves to a root-owned directory outside the workspace (the task statement points there), so builders cannot overwrite or delete it at the build target's path. This adjustment is general, not specific to the task. The bundled documentation is left as shipped: no task-specific corrections.

pricing.note: standard-tier promotional prices, available at least through 2026-11-21; Codex prompts stay under the 272K long-context threshold

decision_rule.cost_parity: Pre-registered 2026-10-05 (README, cost-parity study, expansion), before any run of the expansion; the rule is the study's, pre-registered 2026-10-04. C = the mean model cost of the 5 runs of sol-xhigh-crowbook-single (single worker: GPT-5.6 Sol at xhigh, priced at that experiment's Sol prices). For each loop run of luna-xhigh-crowbook-v1, the parity workspace is the workspace after build k*, the last build whose cumulative cost (builds 1..k and checks 1..k-1, from the Codex transcripts at Luna's prices) does not exceed C; build 1 if build 1 alone exceeds C; the final workspace if the run ends before its cumulative cost reaches C. Outcome on this task: the mean hidden-test pass rate of the 5 Luna parity workspaces against the mean of the 5 Sol single-worker workspaces, each with a 95% percentile bootstrap interval (runs resampled, 10,000 resamples, seed 20260924). Luna outperforms Sol at cost parity if its mean is higher, robustly if the two intervals do not overlap. A run enters only if it completed, its compared workspace was scored on all tests (a workspace that fails to compile or to produce an executable scores 0, as on the leaderboard), neither that workspace contains nor builds the reference executable, and it has no disqualifying audit finding (binary instrumentation, direct model-API calls, proxy use by tools, process-environment reads, web search, changed harness or Codex files). Sensitivity, descriptive: C at Sol's launch prices ($5 input, $0.50 cached input, $30 output per million tokens).
decision_rule.comparison: Luna's loop on the same task: luna-xhigh-crowbook-v1 (5 loop runs) at the cost of these single workers
